subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Numbers, operations and relationships: Place value (numbers between 11 and 50)
source.subtopic: Decompose two-digit numbers into multiples of tens and units/ones to 30 (weeks 1-2), 40 (weeks 3-6) and 50 (weeks 7-10)

show.line: Thirty-six. Three bundles of ten and six loose sticks. Thirty and six make thirty-six!

rounds.prompt: Four bundles of ten and two loose sticks. How many sticks? Tap the number.

rounds.praise: Yes! Two tens and seven ones.

rounds.prompt: Thirty-five. How many tens? Say the number.
Forty and eight. Which number is it?
rounds.praise: Forty-eight! Four tens and eight ones.

rounds.prompt: In the number fifty, how many ones are there?
rounds.praise: Zero ones! Fifty is five tens and no ones.

rounds.prompt: Which number has three tens and one one?

hints: Count the bundles in tens. Then count on the loose ones.
The first digit is the tens. The second digit is the ones.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will break up forty-three.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: Forty-three is four ones and three tens!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! Forty-three is four tens and three ones.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's look together. Four bundles of ten, three loose. Forty-three!

parent_line: Can break a number up to 50 into tens and ones.
